The paper was submitted on December 4, 2016, revised on December 21, 2016, and accepted on December 22, 2016, published in Materials Science Forum Vol. 896, pp 104-110.
The research was conducted at the Science and Technology on Power Beam Processes Laboratory, Beijing Aeronautical Manufacturing Technology Research Institute.
Plasma spraying technology creates coatings with exceptional strength, adherence, and purity through high-temperature and high-velocity particle acceleration.
The composition ratio of spraying powders was Al₂O₃/TiO₂:carbonyl iron:SiO₂ = 8:5:3.
Two coating samples were prepared with thicknesses of 1.0 mm (sample 1#) and 0.5 mm (sample 2#).
Sample 1# achieved an absorption peak of -4.7 dB at 17 GHz with a bandwidth of 16-18 GHz.
Sample 2# achieved an absorption peak of -3 dB at 17.5 GHz with no bandwidth above -4 dB.
The average bonding strength of sample 1# was 23.3 MPa across five measurements.
The average bonding strength of sample 2# was 30.7 MPa across five measurements.
Manual painted coatings typically have bonding strength of approximately 10 MPa.
SiO₂ particles have an average size of approximately 75 micrometers with irregular shape.
SiO₂ has dielectric constant and magnetic permeability that do not change with frequency in the 2-18 GHz range.
Carbonyl iron powder exhibits both magnetic loss and dielectric loss mechanisms for wave absorption.
The plasma spraying current was set at 500 A and voltage at 70 V.
The spraying distance was maintained at 110 mm from the substrate.
The spraying speed was 400 mm/s for both coating samples.
Plasma spray coating can reach temperatures up to 15,000°C, enabling melting of ceramics, metals, and alloys.
Particles cool and solidify within milliseconds upon hitting the substrate.
The coating microstructure shows interlamellar mechanical interlocks, pores, and other features characteristic of thermal spray deposition.
Interfacial polarization between absorbing agents and silica enhances coating absorption performance.
Porosities and cracks in plasma-sprayed coatings provide natural wave-transparent channels.
The study demonstrates that plasma-sprayed coatings have lower electromagnetic absorption than painted coatings but superior mechanical properties.
Automatic control in plasma spraying reduces preparation time compared to manual painting methods.
The coating thickness significantly influences both bonding strength and absorbing properties.
Stealth technology is widely applied to military targets including aircraft, missiles, tanks, submarines, radar stations, and airports.
